title: Denoising Programming Knowledge Tracing with a Code Graph-based Tuning Adaptor

problem.claim: Programming Knowledge Tracking aims to diagnose learners' programming knowledge mastery from coding activities for personalized education.

gap.claim: Existing PKT studies often overlook unrelated-submission signals and weak signals from minor code modifications in long-term programming activity.

contributions.claim: Coda is a code graph-based tuning adaptor for identifying and mitigating noise in existing PKT models.
Coda converts learner code sequences into compact code graphs, uses semantic similarity to identify unwanted signals, and applies a cluster-aware GCN to discriminate and cluster weak signals.
Coda incorporates a lightweight adaptor optimized with two noise feature-based constraints and a navigational regularization term to correct noise-affected knowledge states.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four real-world datasets reportedly show that Coda performs the PKT task in the presence of noisy programming records and outperforms typical baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: PKT diagnoses programming knowledge mastery from coding activities.
Current PKT methods overlook unrelated submissions and weak signals from minor modifications, limiting performance and application.
Coda builds code graphs, identifies unwanted signals through semantic similarity, and clusters weak signals with a cluster-aware GCN.
A constrained, regularized adaptor corrects knowledge states affected by noise and is intended to work with most existing PKT solutions.
The authors report results from four real-world datasets with performance exceeding typical baselines.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four datasets, evaluation metrics, or baseline configurations.
The abstract does not report ablation results or quantify the separate effects of the noise-handling components.
